title: Time-Optimal Sublinear Algorithms for Matching and Vertex Cover
abstract: We study the problem of estimating the size of maximum matching and minimum vertex cover in sublinear time. Denoting the number of vertices by $n$ and the average degree in the graph by $\bar{d}$, we obtain the following results for both problems which are all provably time-optimal up to polylogarithmic factors: * A multiplicative $(2+\epsilon)$-approximation that takes $\tilde{O}(n/\epsilon^2)$ time using adjacency list queries. * A multiplicative-additive $(2, \epsilon n)$-approximation that takes $\tilde{O}((\bar{d} + 1)/\epsilon^2)$ time using adjacency list queries. * A multiplicative-additive $(2, \epsilon n)$-approximation that takes $\tilde{O}(n/\epsilon^3)$ time using adjacency matrix queries. Our main contribution and the key ingredient of the bounds above is a near-tight analysis of the average query complexity of randomized greedy maximal matching which improves upon a seminal result of Yoshida, Yamamoto, and Ito [STOC'09].
